strings.name: Doug Cutting
strings.summary: Doug Cutting works on information retrieval and distributed data software. He developed Lucene, contributed to Nutch and Avro, and cocreated Hadoop with Mike Cafarella, bringing large-scale storage and computation into open software. After Xerox PARC, Apple, Excite and Yahoo, he joined Cloudera. Community collaboration and Apache governance are central to his impact.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Cocreating Hadoop
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Cafarella and the community, he developed distributed storage and processing inspired by Google's systems papers.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Developing Lucene
strings.highlights.h2.text: He opened a reusable Java full-text search library to developers; Apache maintained it for multiple search platforms.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Continuing as Apache chair
strings.timeline.t1.text: The foundation's board appointed him chair again, supporting open-source community governance.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Joining Cloudera
strings.timeline.t2.text: He left Yahoo for the enterprise data-platform company as chief architect.
strings.timeline.t3.title: First Hadoop release
strings.timeline.t3.text: The distributed-computing project separated from Nutch released version 0.1.0.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Nutch joins Apache
strings.timeline.t4.text: The web-search project he created with Cafarella entered the Apache community.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Lucene joins Apache
strings.timeline.t5.text: It became a Jakarta project maintained by volunteer developers.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Open-sourcing Lucene
strings.timeline.t6.text: He released the Java retrieval software developed in his spare time as a reusable search component.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joining Apple research
strings.timeline.t7.text: He developed the V-Twin retrieval engine, later used in Apple products.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Retrieval research at Xerox PARC
strings.timeline.t8.text: He began work on search, linguistic analysis, text summarization and information-access methods.
